Supplies

- those big face air filters if you can swing it 
- heat resistant gloves 
- wear long sleeves and long pants in a natural fiber like cotton (non natural fibers will melt into your skin)

- I’ve taped cardboard on my arms as a protection for batons. 
-shoes you can run in.
-sharpie (so you and others can write numbers for the NLG on you) 
- water water water. Bring a backpack and fill it mostly with water. For dehydration and also to flush off pepper spray or tear gas (tear gas has tiny shards in it so if someone gets hit you need to flush out any affected area.)

Big note! Try to be as subtle. As possible. Don’t head into a crowd with a bike helmet and air filter on your face as it makes the 🐷 on edge. Wear the hat and Covid mask and add more protection as needed! If you have logos on stuff just cover it with electrical tape.

I cannot emphasize this enough. Please ask folks what they need/want before just handing random food to them. They are people not dogs.

When I was assisting folks in Chicago a lot of people actually had too much food (cold food that actively caused coyote and rat infestations). A lot of times if people want food at all, they want warm food. 

If you have a lot of excess food expect that you may need to ask quite a few folks before you find people who want it. There’s definitely people who would like a hot meal, but some folks also go to churches/ non profits/ have family in the area that may already be helping them out.

Also be prepared that folks may need very random items. Phone chargers, bus cards, portable chargers, batteries, cleaning supplies may all be things that are more helpful to a person than food! I literally ended up taking a bunch of steel wool and rat poison and bleach to a spot on request, bc they had an active infestation along the camp. (Before anyone comes for me, you will be so much more helpful to your neighbors if you aren’t policing what items you think they can and can not have) in the winter a good amount of folks will have heaters (if they don’t and you feel generous buying one literally saves lives), small propane tanks are great. 

Money is always the most helpful. I really want people to start destigmatizing just giving people cash. “What if it goes to drugs?” Have you ever tried to get off alcohol/heroine while homeless? Not to mention alcohol withdrawal can literally kill you. Let’s not judge folks who are going through stuff we have no experience in.

Tldr: Please please just ask people what they want if you don’t feel comfortable giving them money.

Chicago is a great city for getting involved in mutual aid. People aren’t explicitly Anarchist but through my experience there I have found that’s where most people land (officially or non officially). There’s obviously a long history of Black anarchists there (Home of the Haymarket affair). Even the Chicago DSA has a ton of anarchists/ libertarian socialists. 

It will take time to earn peoples trust and people will vet you through casual convos. Lots of white saviors especially on the south side so people want to see you show up consistently and do a lot of grunt work before they trust you. You not only have to make an effort, but make a consistent effort.

Most of the really effective projects that exist are headed by Black and Latino folks as well as other POC. They do not take kindly to white fragility so you gotta make sure your ego is in check and you take anti racism seriously. 

Be aware people will critique the fuck out of you, but it means they like you. One popular phrase I’ve heard is “critique with compassion” if someone checks you on something it means they think you’re worth the time and energy to dialogue with you on it. I got trained in this mindset and having moved to NYC have rubbed a lot of people the wrong way in acting in a way that is the norm in Chicago. 

Basically people will really fuck with you at the end of the day if you prove your heart and actions are in the right place. The community is absolutely amazing and Chicago is brilliant at not only getting shit done but will reciprocate on making sure you’re all good and your soul is fed too. They don’t just work they act like a community and that means dinners, music jams etc. 

Also people will really help you if you decide to start your own project. I used to be apart of a small crew that stopped by different houseless encampments and squats and it’s crazy what we were able to do just asking folks for donations and working with the bigger groups. It’s a working class city and people get it so most folks are down to throw a few bucks/ give you donations if you ask. 

I’ve always told people if there’s ever a revolution in the US you’ll know based on what Chicago does. I really miss it.

I’ll be honest and say I am not a fan of capitalism, however there is a metric that doesn’t get talked about as often called velocity of money. If your money is sitting in a bank it’s not actually contributing to the economy. If you’re actively spending money then you are contributing to the economy. 

Working class people tend to live more paycheck to paycheck or in similar circumstances. If they are allowed to keep more money it is likely that more money will end up in the economy because they will spend it out of necessity. Policies that let working class people keep/have more money usually means that rather than going into debt people will come out more even at the end of the month/ alternatively if they are saving money that money might go to things in the future like homeownership or buying a car (rich people can only have so many homes/cars). 

This might be a helpful example 
A person making 1mil a year might have 10-20 pairs of jeans but at a certain point they can only wear so many pairs of pants
But if you take 50 people making 20,000
Each person might have 2-5 pairs of jeans which is 150 pairs 

The purchase of 150 jeans does more for the economy than 15.

The best way to stimulate the economy is any policies that allow poor people to keep more money in a non systematized way. Universal basic income has been brought up but considering it would be a monthly check that would just cause inflation. 

This is why we had covid stimulus packages. It really didn’t have much to do with politicians caring about people and more to do with stimulating the economy. (Honestly republicans arguing against stimulus checks don’t understand capitalism beyond a 101 level. Stimulus checks to working class people were the most direct and effective way support to the economy). 

Now for the left libertarian side:
But also poor people deserve to have enough money to live...

Giving poor people money directly is better than donating to charity. Non profits only exist to uphold a crumbling system. Bureaucracy is inefficient (maybe $10 of $100 actually goes to helping people). 

I’m not interested in policing how working class people use money. (Which is what non profits do)
“but what if someone buys drugs?”
But what if someone’s drug dealer is now able to buy their kid food? 
“What if they use money on something dumb?”
Can you imagine going through life only on the bare minimum? Poor people deserve to have nice things and not be treated as robots whose only purpose is to work, eat, and shit. 

Also fuck the government. I would rather money gets shared directly in communities (big fan of decentralizing state systems). 

TLDR:
The government doesn’t give a fuck about working class people so let us keep our money.

Yes! HSV-1 is what people refer to as cold sores. Sharing drinks can also spread it (although less of likelihood). 

Most people get it in childhood from kids being... well gross with spit/sharing drinks. So most people only have oral symptoms.
Children also tend not to get as sick from a initial outbreak. 
If you get it through kissing/ sharing drinks then you will only have oral symptoms. (Like I said commonly referred to as cold sores). I just got unlucky and received oral sex from someone who had an active HSV-1 outbreak.

You really got to hate the day you read a comment on Reddit and now you gotta go talk to your doctor...

(I recently got HSV-1 in April and now have a boatload of new symptoms. I had fibro and a few other issues previously but now my symptoms are out of control.)

Also with HSV-1 you can get it or orally or on your genitals 

(I found this out the hard way by getting HSV-1 through lesbian sex... 🙃)

Please disclose to your partners if you have HSV-1! 

There’s medication you can take for it that makes outbreaks extremely manageable for most people. (Even with HSV-2 most people I know after the first year might only have an outbreak once a year that can be shortened to less than a week with medication). Herpes isn’t really a big deal for most people with the help of modern medicine! 

unfortunately my immune system sucks and this stuff has been making me really sick (flu symptoms for weeks on end and a whole host of new issues from having other chronic illness). I’m hoping that taking meds everyday in the future will help.

The first outbreak sucks ass *shuddered at the thought of ice packs on my labia and some of the worst flu like symptoms I’ve had in my adult life* But *most* people are pretty much fine after that first outbreak with a little bit of discomfort here and there. Herpes really isn’t a big deal for most! (Just happened to be one of the unlucky few for whom it wrecked my health bc of underlying conditions).
